blocks.text: **Potti Sriramulu (16 March 1901, Madras – 15 December 1952)**: Nellore-rooted railway-trained sanitary engineer who renounced career after family tragedy for Gandhi's ashrams (**Sabarmati's certified inmate; salt satyagraha & individual satyagraha jail terms — 'if I had eleven like Sriramulu, swaraj would come in a year'** (Gandhi's tribute, preserved in the movement's memory)). His pre-1952 cause: **Dalit temple-entry fasts (Nellore, 1946-48** — three fasts securing the Venugopala Swamy temple's opening and Madras-government orders): the Gandhian constructive worker's portfolio. Then the province: with the JVP's Madras-city knot stalling Andhra, **he began his fast on 19 October 1952** at **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** Mylapore house — 58 days, largely ignored by governments — **died 15 December 1952**. The response wrote history: riots swept the Telugu districts (police firings — Anakapalle, Vijayawada deaths), and on **19 December 1952 Nehru announced Andhra State** (minus Madras city).

rows: **11 Telugu districts of Madras** (Circars + Rayalaseema + Nellore); **Kurnool capital** (Sri Bagh's Rayalaseema claim honoured), **High Court at Guntur** — the split-institutions compromise

**CM T. Prakasam** ('Andhra Kesari'), deputy **N. Sanjiva Reddy**; Governor **C.M. Trivedi**; the ministry's instability (fell 1954; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** 1955-56 after mid-term polls) — the young state's teething

**India's first linguistic state** — breached the Dhar-JVP dam; **triggered the SRC (Dec 1953)** and the 1956 all-India linguistic map; proved the fast's terrible arithmetic (a life for a state) and the danger of deferring legitimate demands

Andhra's surrendered claim (Prakasam-era 'Madras manade' sentiment) settled by the JVP price — the grievance's echo shaped Kurnool's choice and later capital anxieties (a straight line to 2014's Hyderabad loss: the state that twice lost its metropolis)

sections.heading: Assessment — the martyr, the method, the meaning

items: **The man**: Sriramulu was no politician — a constructive worker (khadi, Harijan seva, temple-entry) whose moral capital made the fast credible; his Dalit-rights record answers any 'mere linguistic chauvinist' reading — **his last fast demanded the province partly AS an instrument of Harijan uplift** (his stated linkage).

**The method's ethics**: Gandhi had died opposing coercive fasts; Nehru resisted then conceded — the fast-unto-death's double edge (moral appeal vs democratic blackmail) is the evaluative paragraph; the state's silence for 58 days, not the fast alone, killed him — deferral's cost is the counter-argument.

**The meaning**: Amarajeevi ('immortal one') became the linguistic principle's proof-of-blood; every later statehood movement (including Telangana's) cites his precedent — the first linguistic state is thus also the first lesson in **managing identity demands before they find martyrs**.

The dispute over Madras's ownership that stalled Andhra — resolved by JVP's exclusion price, leaving a metropolis-loss wound.
Kurnool-capital/Guntur-HC arrangement honouring Rayalaseema's Sri Bagh claim — sub-regional equity by geography of institutions.
Satyagraha's terminal weapon — morally luminous, democratically double-edged; Sriramulu's case its defining Indian debate.
'Lion of Andhra' — Tanguturi Prakasam, the first CM, famed for baring his chest to police fire (Madras, 1928 Simon protests).

sections.heading: Visalandhra 1956 — the merger and its fine print

blocks.text: The **SRC (1955)** hesitated on merging Telangana (Hyderabad state's Telugu districts) with Andhra — recommending Telangana stay separate until **1961**, with merger only if its assembly consented by 2/3 — citing Telangana's revenue surplus, educational lag and 'Mulki' anxieties. Politics overrode caution: Congress high command + Visalandhra sentiment (the communists' slogan too — 'Visalandhralo Praja Rajyam') produced the **Gentlemen's Agreement (20 Feb 1956, Delhi** — signatories incl. **B. Gopala Reddy, N. Sanjiva Reddy (Andhra); B. Ramakrishna Rao, K.V. Ranga Reddy, M. Chenna Reddy (Telangana)**): safeguards — **Regional Council for Telangana**, domicile ('Mulki') rules in jobs-education, proportionate ministry berths, **Deputy CM from Telangana** (convention), revenue-surplus spending within Telangana. **Andhra Pradesh born 1 November 1956** — Hyderabad capital, **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** first CM (no Telangana deputy appointed: the first breach, day one).

rows: Regional Council toothless; Mulki violations accumulated → **1969 'Jai Telangana'** (Chenna Reddy's Telangana Praja Samithi; ~370 dead in firings; the **8-point/G.O. era**); SC upheld Mulki rules (1972) → Andhra's counter — **1972 'Jai Andhra'** movement → the balancing **Six-Point Formula (1973)**: Mulki rules & Regional Committee gone, **Art 371D** (1973/75 Presidential Order: zonal local-cadre system) + planning board

Green-revolution delta prosperity; Naxalbari's AP edition (Srikakulam 1967-70; later PWG); **NTR's 1982-83 'Telugu atma gauravam'** — TDP ending three-decade Congress rule, federal-politics star; 1990s-2000s: Chandrababu's reform-tech era (Cyberabad, 'Bhagyanagar to byte-nagar'), YSR's welfare era (2004-09 — free power, Aarogyasri, fee reimbursement, Jalayagnam)

**2001: TRS founded (K. Chandrasekhar Rao)** — Telangana's grievances re-armed (water: 'Krishna-Godavari injustice'; jobs: 610 G.O.'s non-implementation; identity); **2004/2009 electoral alliances legitimate the demand**; **KCR's fast (Nov-Dec 2009) → Chidambaram's 9 Dec 2009 statement** → Seemandhra counter-agitation → **Srikrishna Committee (2010**, six options) → prolonged stalemate, Telangana march-crescendos → **CWC decision (July 2013)** → **AP Reorganisation Act (Feb 2014**, passed amid Lok Sabha chaos) → **Telangana born 2 June 2014**

sections.heading: Causes of bifurcation — the analytical core

items: **Broken-safeguards thesis**: Gentlemen's Agreement → day-one breach → Mulki dilutions → 1969 blood → Six-Point substitution → 610 G.O. (1985, on zonal violations) unimplemented — six decades of promissory notes; the constitutional lesson: **safeguards without enforcement machinery are grievance accelerants**.

**Political-economy thesis**: perceived transfer of Telangana's waters (upstream Krishna projects' allocation politics), Hyderabad's growth captured by (in the movement's telling) Seemandhra capital and contractors; jobs & education gaps persisting — 'internal colonialism' as the movement's frame (contested by integrationists citing state-wide schemes).

**Identity-and-agency thesis**: Telangana's distinct dialect-culture (Bathukamma as movement symbol), the 1948-56 Hyderabad-state memory, and a generation's political entrepreneurship (KCR's TRS converting grievance into a single-issue vehicle) — identity supplied the flag; the 2009 fast supplied the trigger; Delhi's oscillation (2009-13) supplied the certainty that only statehood would settle it.

**The verdict frame**: 1956's merger was consent-thin (SRC ignored), 1956-2013's management was enforcement-thin, 2014's parting was process-thin (Assembly's rejected resolution; Art 3's majoritarian speed) — three thin layers, one durable lesson for Indian federalism.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'Born of a breached agreement, AP died of accumulated breaches' — the sentence that frames 1956-2014 as one file. Cite the SRC's original hesitation: the examiner rewards knowing that 1956 itself overrode expert advice.

prelimsPointers: **SRC recommended Telangana remain separate till 1961**, merger only by its assembly's 2/3 consent — overridden politically.
**Gentlemen's Agreement: 20 February 1956** — Regional Council, Mulki-type domicile rules, Deputy-CM convention, ministry proportion, Telangana surplus ring-fenced.
**AP formed 1 November 1956** — first CM **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**; capital Hyderabad; the Deputy-CM convention unhonoured at the start.
**1969 Telangana agitation** (Chenna Reddy's TPS; ~370 killed); **1972 Jai Andhra**; **Six-Point Formula 1973** → **Art 371D (32nd Amendment) & Presidential Order 1975** (zonal cadres).
**G.O. 610 (1985)** — repatriation of non-local appointees in Telangana zones; its non-implementation a standing grievance (Girglani Commission audited it).
**TRS founded 27 April 2001 (KCR)**; **KCR's fast Nov-Dec 2009**; **Chidambaram statement 9 Dec 2009**; **Srikrishna Committee report 30 Dec 2010** (six options).
**AP Reorganisation Act passed Feb 2014** (Assembly's resolution against it notwithstanding — Art 3 procedure); **Telangana: 2 June 2014**.
**NTR founded TDP (29 March 1982)** — CM by January 1983: the Telugu-pride realignment.
